basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Models one performed or attempted procedure occurrence, not the order, plan or procedure definition.
Separates order, readiness, performance, completion, success and complications.
Records safety checks, deviations and non-performance as part of the occurrence.
Links adverse events and reports that keep their own identity.

may: Record performed components, devices and timings from clinical systems.
Check consent, site marking and time-out completion before start.
Link reports, complications and adverse events.
Prepare procedure summaries for clinician sign-off.
mustNot: Start, stop or perform any procedure.
Record a procedure as successful from completed status alone.
Edit a signed procedure record without an amendment.
Omit deviations or complications from the record.
Disclose procedure details outside the care and consent context.
requiresHuman: Consent, indication and the decision to perform a procedure.
Signing the procedure record and reporting adverse events.

considerations: Procedures are invasive; consent and bodily integrity must be respected.
Accurate recording of complications is needed for patient safety and learning.
Some procedures reveal sensitive information about reproduction or identity.

items: A procedure occurrence has a patient, a procedure code, performers, a time, a location, a body site and a status.
It is confused with the order, the procedure definition, a care plan or a diagnostic report.
Wrong-site or wrong-patient procedures from identification errors.
Missed follow-up when complications are not linked.
